In Search of our Missiles

By: Joy Summers | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

Unique Selling Point:
THE SIU HEAD AND INVESTIGATOR WILL SPEAK TO CARTE BLANCHE ABOUT THE STORY
THE INFORMATION IS EXPLOSIVE

Summary:
On the evening of the 3rd March 2021, the SIU’s forensic investigator Zodwa Xesibe, delivered an extraordinary presentation to Members of parliament in a zoom meeting. The subject was the slow and steady collapse of DENEL and a few of the criminal activities that have hastened its demise. At the end of the alarming presentation that has been largely ignored by other journalists, the head of the SIU, advocate Andy Mothibe said it would have looked a lot worse if they had been given a wider scope of investigation by the President.

Around the same time, the union Solidarity, has been embroiled in a dispute with Denel over salary cuts which remains unresolved, and the NGO open secrets reported that Denel was selling weapons to the Saudi’s to bomb Yemen. So it wasn’t a great week for Denel. In fact, it’s been getting steadily worse for Denel, ever since the Gupta’s Salim Essa joined forces with the SOE’s top brass to suck it dry, from around 2015 onwards. The once healthy balance sheet now has R10 billion rand in liabilities -and its weapons intellectual property has been stolen by the Saudi Arabian military industry and a company in the UAE called Halcon.

Finally the SIU is getting to the nuts and bolts of what investigative journalists have been reporting on for the last five years. Now they hope to have this part of their investigation wrapped up by the end of March.



Further information:
So just what did we learn from the SIU forensic investigator Zodwa Xesibe as she detailed the graft for the MP’s? Remember Daniel Mantsha – the lawyer who once defended former president Zuma before he was fired, well he sat at the helm as Chairperson of Denel from 2015 t0 2018. Recently he has been protesting his innocence at the State capture commission, but the SIU presentation suggests otherwise.

Ms. Xesibe explained how Mantsha appointed a Sandton firm of attorneys called Khampa attorneys to the value of R10 million. Apart from the fact that Mantsha broke all the PFMA rules in the appointment, the SIU tells us that he didn’t even use them for Denel work. They were there for the benefit of advancing his own private interests and that of the Gupta’s in defending FIREBLADE – the private passenger terminal at OR TAMBO international. And Mantsha used the group CEO to help him. Khampa say they have earned their money fair and square but when the SIU asked them for records or instruction files they couldn’t provide even a single page! So the SIU is going in hard. Now they want Khampa’s bills to be taxed, they are referring the former CEO for criminal charges and Khampa attorneys to the legal practice council for disciplinary action

VR LASER
Next came their findings on the appointment of VR laser in which they more or less report were irregular in every way, shape and form. They say the process was found to be so fraught with irregularities that any spending with this company was considered irregular expenditure. Mr. Mantsha however still protests his innocence.

It’s clear from 2013 that Salim Essa and the Gupta’s were aligning the stars for maximum looting here. As soon as Essa became the majority shareholder in VR laser, Denel’s senior executives started bumping up the work which was given to VR laser exclusively. Denel’s spending that averaged R13 million a year with VR laser suddenly jumped to R70 and R80 million a year and they were given two ten year contracts that should only expire in 2025. Except that R267 million rand later, the money is gone – hello Dubai, and the SIU doesn’t see much hope in recovering any of it, as VR laser is now in business rescue. According to the SIU only the former group CEO is going to feel the heat. Why Mr. Mantsha gets off is anyone’s guess.

NEXT UP – THE FORMER PREMIER’S SON AND THE JET PILOT BURSARY
They followed up the allegation that three different pilot bursaries were awarded irregularly. It might not be much money, but it’s an abuse of process and taxpayer funds and it shows once again that if you are politically connected, doors open. Except for Oarabile Mahumapelo, son of the former premier of NW, the SIU has now slammed this door shut.

Last week they confirmed publicly that Mahumapelo should not have been awarded R1.56 million rand for a jet pilot programme with 43 air-school. Now the investigators are trying to get back almost R600 000 from Mr. Mahumapelo and another R321 000 from 43 Air-School. They are also trying to get back nearly R800 000 from Ms. Sibulela Damane and the 43 air-school. No one will face any criminal charges, and it seems that only one of the three students ever became a pilot. Good luck to the SIU in getting back these funds.

But the SIU left the best for last. With the help of Denel management and staffers – Saudi Arabia and a company in the UAE have stolen our missile plans and possibly even our missiles

STOLEN MISSILE PLANS AND STOLEN MISSILES.
The SIU dug into the allegation that intellectual property that belonged to Denel was stolen to abet foreign state companies. And what they found was that indeed Denel’s IP has gone to SAMI – the Saudi Arabia Military Industries and Barij dynamics, a company in the UAE that is now known as Halcon. This is what your taxpayer money developed and is now sitting on the Arabian peninsula according to the SIU:

IP of Denel’s air to air missiles; Stand -off weapons; surface target missiles; air defence and unmanned aerial vehicle systems. The data packs that belonged to Denel Dynamics were unlawfully downloaded from Denel’s server to Saudi Arabia military industries and the packs were for Mkhonto, Ingwe and Mokopa missiles. The crime that some may argue is treasonous rather than careless happened in 2018 – likely just before the chairperson resigned, that same Mr. Mantsha that keeps telling us he was looking out for Denel’s best interests.

Then there is the P2 and P3 missiles that the SIU says an official at Denel signed off board minutes authorizing the transfer of the P2 and P3 missiles to Halcon, a company in the UAE.
Interestingly Halcon’s website proudly announced a couple of weeks ago its new air defence missiles – the P31 and P32. So did they just add a 3 to the name and call our missiles their own? They call it a short range guided bomb kit system. In a Carte Blanche investigation we tell this story through the SIU investigation, we go after some of the key players and speak to the ISS to find out just what should happen in a normal democracy when weapons developed by government agencies – are stolen and those responsible seem to just walk away.

Press Release:


Denel’s Detonation

A strategic national asset, key earner of revenue for the country and once-proud inventor of arms and ammunition, state-owned arms company Denel is on its knees. Hollowed out by corruption and mismanagement, it can no longer pay salaries and its projects are at a standstill. Then the Special Investigating Unit briefed Parliament on how Denel’s intellectual property ended up with a Saudi Arabian arms company. Carte Blanche investigates why the institution’s employees have been leaving in droves and what’s become of turnaround plans.

Producer: Joy Summers | Presenter: Masa Kekana

Script:


DENEL FINAL SCRIPT FOR TX SUNDAY 25th APRIL 2021

Commentary One
Not that long ago Denel’s annual reports were glowing.

They told a story of a local State owned company that was a significant international defence manufacturer- that earned more than 50% of its revenue from exports, and had nearly 7000 employees

Link
But not any- more, Denel is on its knees and to give you a clue how that happened, we need to go to Parliament, where the Special Investigating Unit recently briefed stunned MP’s

Commentary Two
This chapter of Denel’s demise was delivered by Zodwa Xesibe, an SIU investigator with more than two decades of forensic experience

Up Sound Zodwa Xesibe
We found that it was necessary to start with the board appointments

She began by explaining how Denel’s demise, started with the appointment of a new board put in place by former minister Lynne Brown.

Up sound Zodwa
And then let me also attend to the issue of budget

Then slide by slide, she explained how money flowed out of Denel – millions to VR laser a Gupta linked company, an allegedly unlawful bursary for a former Premier’s son, and on and on. Head of the SIU, Andy Mothibi, was listening in.

Masa
Now You told parliament that if the scope was widened the SIU findings would have been far worse is that correct?
Andy
Correct it’s our observation, yes.

Commentary Three
He says their investigation showed a direct correlation between corruption and Denel’s demise
Andy
When we presented to parliament, we even presented a picture of the balance sheet of DENEL, and we could determine the time at which it was going down

Commentary Four
Denel is made up of different divisions. Between them they have created the Oryx; the Rooivalk; unmanned drones, vehicles, artillery - and state of the art missiles
Up sound
Missile fired

LINK
It can take eight years to develop a missile, and that’s what the teams at Denel Dynamics did. They were the jewel in the crown, now they don’t even have money for printer cartridges and labels

Commentary Five
For a year staff have been short paid, March salaries weren’t paid, and this latest letter from their CEO, warned Denel Dynamic staff that their April salaries remain at risk.

Darren Olivier is a director of African Defence Review

Darren
So from what I am hearing from inside is that Denel is in serious trouble- skills are leaving at an alarming rate. Entire engineering teams are going

Commentary six
These are the workshops at Denel vehicle systems – once bustling, now nothing is happening. At Solidarity, the trade union has won a court order to seize Denel’s assets. Helgard Cronje is deputy general secretary of the public sector.

Masa
Isn’t that a bit drastic?
Helgard Cronje
Definitely not. If employees are starting to lose their houses, their cars, cannot send their children to school because they don’t have money where does one draw the line? Especially if you have been talking to Denel over the last two years and its board regarding a turnaround strategy it’s not executed.

Masa link
Denel won’t comment, the DPE won’t comment, the only answers we can get are in this statement

Commentary Seven
The Department of Public Enterprises says Denel is not viable in its current form, with a high cost structure, declining revenues and limited export opportunities and that the current liquidity challenge has made it imperative that the state owned company be restructured and repositioned

MASA
What would happen if we continue as we are and these turnaround plans aren’t implemented as a matter of urgency?

Darren
So I think certain parts of Denel are literally months away from collapse, especially Dynamics

Commentary seven A
And he says they cannot trade themselves out of trouble without government’s help

Darren
if things carry on as they are, within 3- 6 months it will be beyond the point of rescue

Commentary eight
Denel is also the original manufacturer for the Oryx and the Rooivalk, used by the SANDF

Darren
If Denel was to go under completely, the Airforce would have no one to maintain those, so what you have with Denel collapsing is not just Denel going down, but perhaps the likelihood of the air-force and other parts of the military would be forced to retire certain aircraft, vehicles and whatever

Commentary nine
The bedrock of Denel’s success was its intellectual capital. Missiles designed and manufactured here, are highly prized on the international market – but then the SIU told parliament that Denel’s missile secrets had been downloaded and given away

Masa
Two Middle Eastern countries are implicated. Who stole our missile plans?
Zodwa
OK, this is not the missiles themselves, but this is the IP that was stolen. The allegations were that some data packs from DENEL IP were downloaded for the SAMI, the Saudi Arabian military industries

Commentary ten
The Saudi Arabian Military Industries is a state owned company with big ambitions. It plans to be one of the world’s top 25 military industries by 2030

Masa
What are data packs?
Zodwa
It’s you know, all the specs to design a missile.

Darren
In theory ...all the rest

Zodwa
Masa
I'm going to read to you the list, that you gave to Parliament of DENEL's air to air missiles that have been taken- that includes standoff weapons, surface target missiles, air defence and unmanned aerial vehicle systems. Is that all correct?





Zodwa
Those were the ones that we are directed to investigate. The SAMI were interested in three specific weapons, it was Umkhonto, it was INGWE, it was MOKOPO and these are now in terms of our findings, these are the data packs that were then downloaded.
Masa
How is this done, because in my head, is it like in the movies where you've got some dude coming into Denel’s offices and then downloading the stuff and giving it to SAMI?
Zodwa
What we know is that one of the executives who resigned from DENEL and who joined the SAMI is the person who instructed a junior employee, an I.T. specialist to download information.
MASA
So the data packs that were downloaded on instruction of this executive to the junior official
Zodwa
Yes...
Masa
Are now the same missiles that the Saudi Arabians have?
Zodwa
Remember, we have not been to the SAMI . We don't know what they have.
Masa
OK, you won't say it, but I smell a rat, obviously.
Zodwa laughs
I can’t read your mind
Masa
I know you can't say it as an investigator, I mean, really, what are the chances that that executive, the SAMI were interested in those missiles, and that's what was downloaded?
Zodwa
we still... the investigation is ongoing Ma’am ...she smiles

Commentary eleven
The SIU is not naming names- but Carte Blanche has written to the former Denel executives who now work at SAMI. We are awaiting their replies.

LINK
It was bad enough that our missile IP ended up with the Saudi Arabian military Industries but it happened a second time – this time in a boardroom

Masa
Now let’s talk about the P2 and P3 missiles?
Zodwa
This one is a different kettle of fish altogether. So these data packs now, this IP was now stolen as a result of a board resolution.

Darren
So the P2 is a small guided unpowered bomb, the P3 is a bomb kit that turns a regular bomb into a smart bomb

Commentary Twelve
The SIU explained that Denel went into a joint venture with a company in the United Arab Emirates – but that company was taken over by arms manufacturer Halcon, in the UAE

Zodwa
Then there was then this board meeting where Halcon demanded the section of the IP that belonged to DENEL for it to be transferred to Halcon. Then one of the key members from the South African company being DENEL, then signed off those rights
Masa
Why?
Zodwa
Without the authority of the board.
Masa
Does that mean Halcon has our P2 and P3 Plans?
Zodwa
That’s correct
Masa
What are they doing with them?
Zodwa
They are busy ..they are making business ....they are in business
Masa
That should be our business!
Zodwa
Yes, even if Denel says tomorrow I pull out of this, they will go out empty handed

Commentary Thirteen
Internal sources within Denel say the P2 and P3 are being sold under different names by Halcon

Darren
the P2 is being marketed as the desert sting, the P3 is marketed as the Thunder p31 and P32
Masa
But it’s ours
Darren
Yes. Both we believe, are in service of the UAE armed forces but I don’t know about exports beyond that

Commentary Fourteen
As the SIU wrap up their investigation, Denel is still reeling from corruption. And as it collapses its taking with it jobs and skills, and furthering our deindustrialisation

Zodwa
This a serious crime against the state.

Hollowed out by corruption and mismanagement, it can no longer pay salaries and its projects are at a standstill. Then the Special Investigating Unit briefed Parliament on how Denel’s intellectual property ended up with a Saudi Arabian arms company. Carte Blanche investigates why the institution’s employees have been leaving in droves and what’s become of turnaround plans. Producer: Joy Summers | Presenter: Masa Kekana Script: DENEL FINAL SCRIPT FOR TX SUNDAY 25th APRIL 2021 Commentary One Not that long ago Denel’s annual reports were glowing. They told a story of a local State owned company that was a significant international defence manufacturer- that earned more than 50% of its revenue from exports, and had nearly 7000 employees Link But not any- more, Denel is on its knees and to give you a clue how that happened, we need to go to Parliament, where the Special Investigating Unit recently briefed stunned MP’s Commentary Two This chapter of Denel’s demise was delivered by Zodwa Xesibe, an SIU investigator with more than two decades of forensic experience Up Sound Zodwa Xesibe We found that it was necessary to start with the board appointments She began by explaining how Denel’s demise, started with the appointment of a new board put in place by former minister Lynne Brown. Up sound Zodwa And then let me also attend to the issue of budget Then slide by slide, she explained how money flowed out of Denel – millions to VR laser a Gupta linked company, an allegedly unlawful bursary for a former Premier’s son, and on and on. Head of the SIU, Andy Mothibi, was listening in. Masa Now You told parliament that if the scope was widened the SIU findings would have been far worse is that correct? Andy Correct it’s our observation, yes. Commentary Three He says their investigation showed a direct correlation between corruption and Denel’s demise Andy When we presented to parliament, we even presented a picture of the balance sheet of DENEL, and we could determine the time at which it was going down Commentary Four Denel is made up of different divisions. Between them they have created the Oryx; the Rooivalk; unmanned drones, vehicles, artillery - and state of the art missiles Up sound Missile fired LINK It can take eight years to develop a missile, and that’s what the teams at Denel Dynamics did. They were the jewel in the crown, now they don’t even have money for printer cartridges and labels Commentary Five For a year staff have been short paid, March salaries weren’t paid, and this latest letter from their CEO, warned Denel Dynamic staff that their April salaries remain at risk. Darren Olivier is a director of African Defence Review Darren So from what I am hearing from inside is that Denel is in serious trouble- skills are leaving at an alarming rate. Entire engineering teams are going Commentary six These are the workshops at Denel vehicle systems – once bustling, now nothing is happening. At Solidarity, the trade union has won a court order to seize Denel’s assets. Helgard Cronje is deputy general secretary of the public sector. Masa Isn’t that a bit drastic? Helgard Cronje Definitely not. If employees are starting to lose their houses, their cars, cannot send their children to school because they don’t have money where does one draw the line? Especially if you have been talking to Denel over the last two years and its board regarding a turnaround strategy it’s not executed. Masa link Denel won’t comment, the DPE won’t comment, the only answers we can get are in this statement Commentary Seven The Department of Public Enterprises says Denel is not viable in its current form, with a high cost structure, declining revenues and limited export opportunities and that the current liquidity challenge has made it imperative that the state owned company be restructured and repositioned MASA What would happen if we continue as we are and these turnaround plans aren’t implemented as a matter of urgency? Darren So I think certain parts of Denel are literally months away from collapse, especially Dynamics Commentary seven A And he says they cannot trade themselves out of trouble without government’s help Darren if things carry on as they are, within 3- 6 months it will be beyond the point of rescue Commentary eight Denel is also the original manufacturer for the Oryx and the Rooivalk, used by the SANDF Darren If Denel was to go under completely, the Airforce would have no one to maintain those, so what you have with Denel collapsing is not just Denel going down, but perhaps the likelihood of the air-force and other parts of the military would be forced to retire certain aircraft, vehicles and whatever Commentary nine The bedrock of Denel’s success was its intellectual capital. Missiles designed and manufactured here, are highly prized on the international market – but then the SIU told parliament that Denel’s missile secrets had been downloaded and given away Masa Two Middle Eastern countries are implicated. Who stole our missile plans? Zodwa OK, this is not the missiles themselves, but this is the IP that was stolen. The allegations were that some data packs from DENEL IP were downloaded for the SAMI, the Saudi Arabian military industries Commentary ten The Saudi Arabian Military Industries is a state owned company with big ambitions. It plans to be one of the world’s top 25 military industries by 2030 Masa What are data packs? Zodwa It’s you know, all the specs to design a missile. Darren In theory ...all the rest Zodwa Masa I'm going to read to you the list, that you gave to Parliament of DENEL's air to air missiles that have been taken- that includes standoff weapons, surface target missiles, air defence and unmanned aerial vehicle systems. Is that all correct? Zodwa Those were the ones that we are directed to investigate. The SAMI were interested in three specific weapons, it was Umkhonto, it was INGWE, it was MOKOPO and these are now in terms of our findings, these are the data packs that were then downloaded. Masa How is this done, because in my head, is it like in the movies where you've got some dude coming into Denel’s offices and then downloading the stuff and giving it to SAMI? Zodwa What we know is that one of the executives who resigned from DENEL and who joined the SAMI is the person who instructed a junior employee, an I.T. specialist to download information. MASA So the data packs that were downloaded on instruction of this executive to the junior official Zodwa Yes... Masa Are now the same missiles that the Saudi Arabians have? Zodwa Remember, we have not been to the SAMI . We don't know what they have. Masa OK, you won't say it, but I smell a rat, obviously. Zodwa laughs I can’t read your mind Masa I know you can't say it as an investigator, I mean, really, what are the chances that that executive, the SAMI were interested in those missiles, and that's what was downloaded? Zodwa we still... the investigation is ongoing Ma’am ...she smiles Commentary eleven The SIU is not naming names- but Carte Blanche has written to the former Denel executives who now work at SAMI. We are awaiting their replies. LINK It was bad enough that our missile IP ended up with the Saudi Arabian military Industries but it happened a second time – this time in a boardroom Masa Now let’s talk about the P2 and P3 missiles? Zodwa This one is a different kettle of fish altogether. So these data packs now, this IP was now stolen as a result of a board resolution. Darren So the P2 is a small guided unpowered bomb, the P3 is a bomb kit that turns a regular bomb into a smart bomb Commentary Twelve The SIU explained that Denel went into a joint venture with a company in the United Arab Emirates – but that company was taken over by arms manufacturer Halcon, in the UAE Zodwa Then there was then this board meeting where Halcon demanded the section of the IP that belonged to DENEL for it to be transferred to Halcon. Then one of the key members from the South African company being DENEL, then signed off those rights Masa Why? Zodwa Without the authority of the board. Masa Does that mean Halcon has our P2 and P3 Plans? Zodwa That’s correct Masa What are they doing with them? Zodwa They are busy ..they are making business ....they are in business Masa That should be our business! Zodwa Yes, even if Denel says tomorrow I pull out of this, they will go out empty handed Commentary Thirteen Internal sources within Denel say the P2 and P3 are being sold under different names by Halcon Darren the P2 is being marketed as the desert sting, the P3 is marketed as the Thunder p31 and P32 Masa But it’s ours Darren Yes. Both we believe, are in service of the UAE armed forces but I don’t know about exports beyond that Commentary Fourteen As the SIU wrap up their investigation, Denel is still reeling from corruption. And as it collapses its taking with it jobs and skills, and furthering our deindustrialisation Zodwa This a serious crime against the state. metadata.Unique Selling Point: THE SIU HEAD AND INVESTIGATOR WILL SPEAK TO CARTE BLANCHE ABOUT THE STORY THE INFORMATION IS EXPLOSIVE
metadata.Summary: On the evening of the 3rd March 2021, the SIU’s forensic investigator Zodwa Xesibe, delivered an extraordinary presentation to Members of parliament in a zoom meeting. The subject was the slow and steady collapse of DENEL and a few of the criminal activities that have hastened its demise. At the end of the alarming presentation that has been largely ignored by other journalists, the head of the SIU, advocate Andy Mothibe said it would have looked a lot worse if they had been given a wider scope of investigation by the President. Around the same time, the union Solidarity, has been embroiled in a dispute with Denel over salary cuts which remains unresolved, and the NGO open secrets reported that Denel was selling weapons to the Saudi’s to bomb Yemen. So it wasn’t a great week for Denel. In fact, it’s been getting steadily worse for Denel, ever since the Gupta’s Salim Essa joined forces with the SOE’s top brass to suck it dry, from around 2015 onwards. The once healthy balance sheet now has R10 billion rand in liabilities -and its weapons intellectual property has been stolen by the Saudi Arabian military industry and a company in the UAE called Halcon. Finally the SIU is getting to the nuts and bolts of what investigative journalists have been reporting on for the last five years. Now they hope to have this part of their investigation wrapped up by the end of March.
metadata.Further information: So just what did we learn from the SIU forensic investigator Zodwa Xesibe as she detailed the graft for the MP’s? Remember Daniel Mantsha – the lawyer who once defended former president Zuma before he was fired, well he sat at the helm as Chairperson of Denel from 2015 t0 2018. Recently he has been protesting his innocence at the State capture commission, but the SIU presentation suggests otherwise. Ms. Xesibe explained how Mantsha appointed a Sandton firm of attorneys called Khampa attorneys to the value of R10 million. Apart from the fact that Mantsha broke all the PFMA rules in the appointment, the SIU tells us that he didn’t even use them for Denel work. They were there for the benefit of advancing his own private interests and that of the Gupta’s in defending FIREBLADE – the private passenger terminal at OR TAMBO international. And Mantsha used the group CEO to help him. Khampa say they have earned their money fair and square but when the SIU asked them for records or instruction files they couldn’t provide even a single page! So the SIU is going in hard. Now they want Khampa’s bills to be taxed, they are referring the former CEO for criminal charges and Khampa attorneys to the legal practice council for disciplinary action VR LASER Next came their findings on the appointment of VR laser in which they more or less report were irregular in every way, shape and form. They say the process was found to be so fraught with irregularities that any spending with this company was considered irregular expenditure. Mr. Mantsha however still protests his innocence. It’s clear from 2013 that Salim Essa and the Gupta’s were aligning the stars for maximum looting here. As soon as Essa became the majority shareholder in VR laser, Denel’s senior executives started bumping up the work which was given to VR laser exclusively. Denel’s spending that averaged R13 million a year with VR laser suddenly jumped to R70 and R80 million a year and they were given two ten year contracts that should only expire in 2025. Except that R267 million rand later, the money is gone – hello Dubai, and the SIU doesn’t see much hope in recovering any of it, as VR laser is now in business rescue. According to the SIU only the former group CEO is going to feel the heat. Why Mr. Mantsha gets off is anyone’s guess. NEXT UP – THE FORMER PREMIER’S SON AND THE JET PILOT BURSARY They followed up the allegation that three different pilot bursaries were awarded irregularly. It might not be much money, but it’s an abuse of process and taxpayer funds and it shows once again that if you are politically connected, doors open. Except for Oarabile Mahumapelo, son of the former premier of NW, the SIU has now slammed this door shut. Last week they confirmed publicly that Mahumapelo should not have been awarded R1.56 million rand for a jet pilot programme with 43 air-school. Now the investigators are trying to get back almost R600 000 from Mr. Mahumapelo and another R321 000 from 43 Air-School. They are also trying to get back nearly R800 000 from Ms. Sibulela Damane and the 43 air-school. No one will face any criminal charges, and it seems that only one of the three students ever became a pilot. Good luck to the SIU in getting back these funds. But the SIU left the best for last. With the help of Denel management and staffers – Saudi Arabia and a company in the UAE have stolen our missile plans and possibly even our missiles STOLEN MISSILE PLANS AND STOLEN MISSILES. The SIU dug into the allegation that intellectual property that belonged to Denel was stolen to abet foreign state companies. And what they found was that indeed Denel’s IP has gone to SAMI – the Saudi Arabia Military Industries and Barij dynamics, a company in the UAE that is now known as Halcon. This is what your taxpayer money developed and is now sitting on the Arabian peninsula according to the SIU: IP of Denel’s air to air missiles; Stand -off weapons; surface target missiles; air defence and unmanned aerial vehicle systems. The data packs that belonged to Denel Dynamics were unlawfully downloaded from Denel’s server to Saudi Arabia military industries and the packs were for Mkhonto, Ingwe and Mokopa missiles. The crime that some may argue is treasonous rather than careless happened in 2018 – likely just before the chairperson resigned, that same Mr. Mantsha that keeps telling us he was looking out for Denel’s best interests. Then there is the P2 and P3 missiles that the SIU says an official at Denel signed off board minutes authorizing the transfer of the P2 and P3 missiles to Halcon, a company in the UAE. Interestingly Halcon’s website proudly announced a couple of weeks ago its new air defence missiles – the P31 and P32. So did they just add a 3 to the name and call our missiles their own? They call it a short range guided bomb kit system. In a Carte Blanche investigation we tell this story through the SIU investigation, we go after some of the key players and speak to the ISS to find out just what should happen in a normal democracy when weapons developed by government agencies – are stolen and those responsible seem to just walk away.
